DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Exacerbation.

The combination of a significant smoking history, a confirmed obstructive pattern on spirometry (FEV1/FVC < 0.70), and symptoms triggered by a recent upper respiratory infection strongly supports this diagnosis. The negative findings for chest pain and palpitations help rule out acute cardiac causes, and the "normal readings" in your latest measurement appear to be an error given the definitive spirometry results.
